# CPython 3.13 Free Threading and Extension Imports

CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading as a configuration in which the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) can be disabled. What happens at runtime also depends on the extensions an application imports.

When an extension is imported without an explicit declaration that it supports free threading, CPython issues a warning and enables the GIL. The way to make that declaration differs between extensions using multi-phase initialization and those using single-phase initialization.

Declaring support signals compatibility with the free-threading runtime mode. It is separate from making the extension’s code thread-safe: the declaration alone does not establish that the code is safe to use across threads.
